## The MATISSE short course

**Video:** [Watch the MATISSE course tour on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CLSP755kp4I) (2 min 8 sec).

Learn to prepare data, explore cancer rates, and use **age-period-cohort (APC) methods**. These methods describe patterns by age, calendar period, and birth cohort. A birth cohort is a group of people born in the same year or years.

**Live sessions** — planned for late October 2026 (exact dates to be confirmed):

-   **Day 1 — Overview and APC primer.** Learn the basic APC concepts. Tour the course page and prepare data for the NCI APC web tool.
-   **Day 2 — How to move forward.** Explore comparative methods and SAGE. Review the main ideas behind the methods and when to use them.
-   **Optional follow-up.** Join a smaller session to discuss the theory and methods in more detail. Drop in for the topics you need.

Time is set aside for Q&A at the end of each session.

**On-demand sessions** will provide step-by-step practice on YouTube. Follow each lecture with the matching MATLAB live script (`.mlx`). A live script combines explanations, code, and results in one file. Recordings of the live sessions will be added when available.

This course is for epidemiologists, cancer registry researchers, and biostatisticians. Start with [Getting started with MATLAB Online](getting-started.html#getting-started-with-matlab-online). Then open the Overview live script in [Downloads](resources.html#downloads). Use the [FAQ](resources.html#faq) for common questions.

## What you'll learn

-   Set up MATISSE in MATLAB Online.
-   Explore rates by age and calendar period.
-   Draw and compare Lexis diagrams.
-   Find APC methods and supporting resources.

Philip S. Rosenberg, PhD, developed the MATISSE toolbox and its code. The toolbox implements methods developed with the cancer surveillance research community. These include the APC methods described in Filho & Rosenberg, Front Oncol 2024. The team listed above develops the course.
